posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
For those looking to make a alluminum can table, I have found a brewery that will gladly ship palets of cans, or any amount, of sealed cans with only air in them. This makes the can very strong compared to an open can.

Email me if you need his contact information.

posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md: I'm interested. I'm in the process now of building a larger can table and sure hope to have it done by PCGGIII. When finished it will have 319 cans. The empty cans are epoxied to the top and bottom skins thus sealing the air inside. Would there really be an advantage using the cans with the air already in them?

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: If you try to dent a can with liquid in them you will see how much stronger the can is when it holds pressure. Air cans are much more durable. 319 is not very many. When I was looking I wanted 4x8' and 3 cans high! So buying air cans is also easier than collecting 1700 cans or whatever it worked out to.
